Title: ICJ rules Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya in 2017
Article:
GENEVA: The United Nations' top court ruled Thursday that Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya Muslims in 2017, marking the first time it has held a state responsible for genocide, Anadolu Ajansi (AA) reported.
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) found Myanmar responsible for genocide during military operations in northern Rakhine State by a vote of 9-6.
Reading the judgment, International Court of Justice President Judge Yuji Iwasawa said Myanmar "has committed genocide against the Rohingya group in northern Rakhine State, in violation of its obligations under the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide".
"The court finds that Myanmar's security forces killed thousands of Rohingya civilians, perpetrated widespread acts of sexual violence, as well as acts of extreme violence against children, and attacked fleeing Rohingya as they sought to flee in large numbers to Bangladesh," the court said.
The judges found that Myanmar's security forces committed acts prohibited under the Genocide Convention with "an intent to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population of Myanmar".
The court concluded that the scale and methods of the violence went beyond military necessity and reflected "an intent to destroy a substantial part of the group".
In a separate 9-6 vote, the court found that Myanmar had violated its obligation to prevent genocide committed by civilians acting alongside its security forces.
It also found that Myanmar had failed to fulfil its obligation to punish genocide.
The court ordered Myanmar to take "immediate and effective steps" to investigate suspected perpetrators and facilitate the "safe, voluntary, and dignified return" of displaced Rohingya.
Myanmar must also restore or replace lost or damaged Rohingya property and provide physical and psychological rehabilitation to those injured, according to the judgment.
The ruling further requires Myanmar to compensate Rohingya victims for damage that cannot be remedied through restitution.
The court gave Myanmar two years to report on restitution measures, while compensation arrangements will be determined in subsequent proceedings.
– Bernama-Anadolu

Title: GPS welcomes Pas decision to sit out Sarawak election
Article:
KUCHING: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) has welcomed Pas' decision to sit out the Sarawak election.
GPS information chief Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said the decision reflected a spirit of solidarity, particularly in preserving relations between political parties and communities in Sarawak.
Before the announcement, Karim said he had learnt that Pas was keen to contest in Semariang, Sebuyau and Beting Maro.
"This is a show of solidarity. We all know that when they (Pas) wanted to contest, they were not targeting urban areas, but areas with a Malay majority.
"Why divide the ummah?" he told reporters at a food basket distribution programme in Kampung Moyan Laut, Asajaya, today.
Karim, who is the Asajaya assemblyman, said GPS would appreciate it if Pas' decision was motivated by a desire to unite Muslims.
He also welcomed Umno and Barisan Nasional's decision not to field candidates in the Sarawak election.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi
had previously said the decision
was made in line with a political understanding between Umno and GPS lynchpin Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu.
Karim said political relationships should not change according to convenience, particularly when a party sought to forge a partnership after an election despite having opposed its rivals during the campaign.
He said the effects of a two-week campaign could linger long after the election, particularly when local communities had to continue living together after political leaders from Peninsular Malaysia returned home.
"If we quarrel because of a two-week campaign, it could drag on and cause people in the villages to remain at odds for much longer.
"Those who spread slander and pit us against one another will leave. This is what we do not want," he said.
Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan confirmed that the party had decided to sit out the
Sarawak election
after taking into account current political developments and various other considerations.
He said Pas remained committed to strengthening unity, political stability and public well-being, in line with the party's policies and principles.
The 13th Sarawak election will involve 82 state assembly seats, with nomination day set for Nov 28, early voting on Dec 8 and polling on Dec 12.

Title: ART with US yet to take effect pending Washington's amendments
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Agreement on Reciprocal Trade (ART) between Malaysia and the United States has yet to take effect, with Malaysia awaiting amendments from Washington, the Dewan Rakyat was told.
Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said the US would propose amendments to references to the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) and reciprocal tariffs in the agreement.
"Until now, the ART has not yet taken effect following the US Supreme Court decision in February 2026 that annulled the implementation of reciprocal tariffs under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA).
"The US side will submit an amending protocol to Malaysia once the document is finalised. Malaysia is awaiting the amending protocol before taking further action," he said when winding up the committee-stage debate on the ministry's allocation under the 2027 Budget in Parliament.
He said the ART, signed on Oct 26, 2025, with US President Donald Trump on the sidelines of the 47th Asean Summit here, did not prevent Malaysia from working with other countries on critical minerals and rare earths.
"Generally, the ART does not impose any restriction on Malaysia to establish or continue cooperation in critical minerals and rare earths with any country.
"The provisions also do not contain any requirement that cooperation in those areas be carried out exclusively with the United States," he said.
He said Malaysia was also not required to obtain the United States' consent or approval before entering into such cooperation with other countries.
He rejected a claim made by Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal (PN-Machang) during the debate.
"So what Machang said is not correct. Accordingly, Malaysia retains room to cooperate with other countries in critical minerals and rare earths, subject to Malaysian laws and policies in force," he said.
Datuk Dr Ku Abd Rahman Ku Ismail (PN-Kubang Pasu) asked whether the Democratic Party's wins in the US midterm elections, which he said gave it control of both chambers of Congress, would affect the ART.
"The reality is the president is still Donald Trump, and whatever the politics, we have to wait and see," Sim said.

Title: Denza D9 gets RM345,800 upgrade
Article:
DENZA Malaysia has introduced an updated D9 Prestige AWD priced at RM345,800, with changes to its cabin, entertainment system, safety equipment and electric powertrain as competition in the premium electric multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) segment grows.
The latest version retains the model's all-wheel-drive electric drivetrain but gains a 115.07kWh second-generation Blade Battery, with a claimed driving range of up to 650km under the New European Driving Cycle (NEDC).
The battery supports BYD Flash Charging, allowing the vehicle to charge from 10 per cent to 70 per cent in five minutes and from 10 per cent to 97 per cent in nine minutes under optimal conditions, when connected to compatible charging infrastructure.
Power output is rated at 410kW, equivalent to 557PS, with 445Nm of torque.
The vehicle also receives a dual-valve DiSus-C intelligent damping system, which adjusts suspension response to improve ride comfort and handling.
Cabin changes include Nappa leather upholstery, 14-way adjustable second-row seats with 16-point massage functions, and heating and ventilation for both second- and third-row seats.
The third row also gains four-way power adjustment.
Rear passengers get two 12.8-inch multimedia screens, while the audio system has been upgraded to a 16-speaker Devialet setup.
The MPV offers 689 litres of luggage capacity with all seats in place, rising to 2,436 litres with the seats configured for additional storage. It also has 126 litres of underfloor storage.
Safety equipment includes autonomous emergency braking, intelligent cruise control and emergency lane-keeping assist. A front centre airbag brings the total number of airbags to nine.
The updated model is priced at RM345,800, excluding insurance and registration, and comes in four exterior colours: Arctic White, Cosmos Black, Starry Night Grey and Whale Blue Sea.
The standard ownership package includes a six-year or 150,000km vehicle warranty, an eight-year or 160,000km high-voltage battery warranty, and six years of complimentary scheduled maintenance.
"Malaysia is an important market for Denza. Every enhancement has been made with the customer experience in mind, from greater cabin comfort to improved entertainment and technology," said BYD Malaysia managing director Jacob Ma.
"We want the D9 to be more than just a luxury MPV, but a space where families and passengers can truly enjoy the journey together.
"Combined with the BYD Second Generation Blade Battery and BYD Flash Charging capability, the new D9 brings together comfort, technology and convenience in a way that we believe will make a real difference to our customers," Ma added.

Title: Home Ministry open to reviewing Rela firearms policy to help farmers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Home Ministry is prepared to review the mechanism governing the use of firearms by Malaysian Volunteer Corps (Rela) personnel to help farmers tackle crop pests and wildlife threats, which have caused mounting losses to the agriculture sector.
Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Dr Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said the review would cover firearm approvals and usage, including eligibility requirements, types of authorisation and usage limits, subject to the jurisdiction of the police and relevant laws.
He said selected Rela personnel who passed security screening had previously been issued shotguns to assist with local security duties and operations to control crop pests.
However, the practice was discontinued following cases of firearm misuse and accidents, as well as a review of firearm procedures following Rela's transformation under the Malaysian Volunteer Corps Act 2012.
"Rela can still assist in joint operations to control crop pests involving the Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) and local communities.
"Its role is limited to logistical support, perimeter security, cordoning off areas, setting traps and other permitted assistance. Shooting wildlife as a last resort is carried out by authorised Perhilitan enforcement officers," he said during a Special Chamber sitting in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Shamsul Anuar was responding to Datuk Rosol Wahid (PN-Hulu Terengganu), who proposed that the government review the policy on Rela's role in tackling crop pests, including allowing qualified personnel to possess and use firearms under controlled conditions.
Rosol said records from the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) showed that 76,361 wildlife conflict complaints were recorded nationwide from 2021 to May this year, with estimated losses amounting to RM58.7 million, affecting farmers' incomes and national food security.
Shamsul Anuar said the ministry understood the difficulties faced by farmers due to wildlife such as wild boars, macaques and elephants destroying crops, reducing their income and posing safety risks to rural communities and those living near forests.
Any proposal to expand Rela's role, he added, would require careful consideration of farmers' needs, public safety and wildlife conservation.
He said Home Ministry would focus on four key areas, including strengthening integrated operations led by Perhilitan, with assessments of threat levels and high-risk areas.
The ministry would also review firearm authorisation, identify Rela personnel with the necessary competence, experience and safety training, and establish joint standard operating procedures (SOPs) among the agencies involved.
Any proposal to allow Rela personnel to use firearms must comply with the Malaysian Volunteer Corps Act 2012, the Arms Act 1960 and the Wildlife Conservation Act 2010.
Home Ministry would also coordinate discussions with NRES, particularly Perhilitan, and police to refine an appropriate cooperation mechanism.
Shamsul Anuar said Home Ministry had taken note that Hulu Terengganu had 830 active Rela personnel out of 25,322 registered members in the district as at Oct 30, 2026.
"This existing personnel strength could be considered when planning support in identified areas requiring intervention," he said.

Title: Magnum's Q3 net profit more than doubles to RM49.9mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Magnum Bhd's net profit more than doubled to RM49.91 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM24.53 million a year ago, despite lower revenue.
Revenue declined 1.49 per cent to RM521.58 million from RM529.46 million, dragged down by its gaming division.
Gaming revenue fell RM7.9 million to RM521.6 million from RM529.4 million, despite the division conducting 42 draws compared with 40 a year ago.
The division's pre-tax profit rose to RM78.5 million from RM39 million, mainly due to lower prize payouts.
For the nine-month period, Magnum's net profit rose 18.09 per cent to RM161.11 million from RM136.43 million a year ago, while revenue fell 5.71 per cent to RM1.65 billion from RM1.75 billion.
On prospects, Magnum said it remained cautiously optimistic about its gaming business for the final quarter of the financial year.
The company said illegal gaming activities, cost-of-living pressures and cautious consumer sentiment, compounded by heightened geopolitical uncertainties arising from tensions in the Middle East, were likely to continue weighing on customers' discretionary spending.
The group said it would continue to strengthen customer engagement and improve operational efficiency through its retail network and digital initiatives.
Barring unforeseen circumstances, Magnum expects these efforts, alongside disciplined cost management, to support its performance for the remainder of the financial year.

Title: Chinese EVs test Japan's hybrid stronghold
Article:
JAPAN's technology-neutral approach to vehicle electrification has helped conventional hybrids retain their dominance.
This has slowed the shift towards battery-electric vehicles (BEVs) and plug-in hybrids (PHEVs), according to BMI automotive team at a recent webinar.
BMI said Japan's target of having all new passenger car sales electrified by 2035 does not require a wholesale shift to plug-in vehicles. The definition includes conventional hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), BEVs, PHEVs and fuel-cell electric vehicles (FCEVs).
This contrasts with the European Union and the United Kingdom, where regulations place greater emphasis on zero-tailpipe-emission vehicles, effectively favouring BEVs.
Japan's policy has reinforced the position of domestic automakers with established hybrid technology, reducing pressure on manufacturers and consumers to switch rapidly to fully electric or plug-in models.
However, BMI expects the growing presence of Chinese EV manufacturers to intensify competition for Japanese automakers, particularly through their strong price-to-value proposition.
The pressure could accelerate BEV development among Japanese manufacturers as they seek to defend their market positions.
BYD's Racco, an electric vehicle developed specifically for Japan's strategically important kei-car segment, illustrates how Chinese manufacturers are adapting their products to local market requirements.
The move could also prompt Japanese automakers to accelerate development of their own electric kei cars, BMI said.
Despite the competitive challenge, Chinese brands are expected to gain market share in Japan only gradually, given the strength of domestic manufacturers and their established dealership and distribution networks.
The bigger threat to Japanese automakers is likely to come from overseas markets, particularly Southeast Asia, Latin America, Europe and sub-Saharan Africa, where Chinese manufacturers are expanding rapidly.
In these regions, Chinese brands are increasingly competing directly with Japanese manufacturers, challenging their longstanding strengths in affordability, reliability and distribution.
For Japanese automakers, the competitive pressure is therefore not confined to the pace of electrification at home.
Their ability to defend overseas market share will increasingly depend on how quickly they can respond to Chinese rivals on pricing, technology and product development.
BMI's assessment suggests that while Japan's policy framework will continue to support hybrids in the near term, competition abroad could become a stronger catalyst for the country's automakers to accelerate their electric vehicle strategies.

Title: Wan Ahmad Dahlan retires after 31 years in public service
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz today retired as the 27th director-general of the Public Service Department (PSD), ending a 31-year career spanning several key government institutions.
"I have just a few hours left before concluding my service, marking more than 31 years in the public service.
"I am grateful that in every posting, I had a great team, whether at the National Palace, Home Affairs Ministry, Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU) or PSD," he said.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan, who turns 60 tomorrow, joined the public service on Jan 25, 1995. He was appointed PSD director-general on Jan 8, 2024.
Speaking to reporters after his farewell ceremony today, he described the introduction of the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA) as one of his major achievements.
He said its implementation required balancing civil servants' needs with the government's financial capacity.
He said cooperation between the department, stakeholders and the Congress of Unions of Employees in the Public and Civil Services (Cuepacs) had been instrumental in making the system a success.
"What stands out most to me is the success my team at PSD and I achieved in completing the new remuneration system, namely the SSPA.
"It was not easy, as it required balancing the needs of civil servants with the government's financial capacity.
"Nevertheless, through the cooperation of all parties, including Cuepacs, which represents public service associations and trade unions, we were able to bring it to fruition.
"Civil servants are now enjoying the benefits outlined under the SSPA," he said.
The
SSPA
was introduced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in August 2024 to replace the Malaysian Remuneration System. It took effect on Dec 1 that year.
He also cited the Government Service Efficiency Commitment Act 2025 (ILTIZAM Act), which came into force on Dec 1 last year, as another significant achievement.
The Act requires ministries and departments to review existing legislation, standard operating procedures and administrative processes to reduce red tape, eliminate overlapping regulations and ease regulatory burdens.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan said the initiative aimed to transform the government's role from regulator to enabler while ensuring public services kept pace with changing needs.
"Another source of satisfaction for me is our success in introducing the ILTIZAM Act, under which all ministries and departments are required to review existing Acts, SOPs and procedures and replace those no longer suited to current circumstances," he said.
He said the reviews must be presented to Parliament every three years to demonstrate improvements in public service delivery.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan said he hoped Malaysia's public service would achieve standards comparable with those of developed nations, including the United States, Singapore and European countries.
He said the country was moving in the right direction, with civil servants' commitment and determination being key to achieving that goal.
"My hope is to see Malaysia's public service stand on par with that of developed nations such as the United States, European countries and, closest to home, Singapore.
"I believe that with commitment and a strong drive among civil servants, we will succeed in standing shoulder to shoulder with these developed nations," he said.
He said public service delivery must remain people-centric, with government policies translating into tangible improvements in people's lives.
"Whatever we implement, the policies we execute must be people-centric.
"Let what we implement not merely remain policies on paper within ministries and departments, but be felt by the people. That is what matters most," he said.
In an accompanying statement, PSD said it had strengthened performance management through MyPerformance, with the Public Service Engagement Index rising from 78.5 per cent in 2023 to 84.37 per cent in 2024.
The department had also studied the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) and audited staffing positions to modernise work processes and reduce overlapping duties.
Public feedback gathered through its e-Participation platform and Customer Satisfaction Surveys was also used to improve service delivery.
In his farewell message, Wan Ahmad Dahlan called on PSD personnel to uphold the H.E.M.A.T. values by simplifying processes for stakeholders, aligning work practices with government priorities and expediting assigned tasks.
He also called for stronger collaboration with academia and greater engagement on the ground.
He urged the department's leadership to provide constructive guidance and discharge their responsibilities fairly and compassionately.
He thanked Anwar for entrusting him with leading the country's public service, which has about 1.5 million personnel.
"It is no easy feat to cater to the needs of every scheme within the public service.
"However, with the formidable teams we have at PSD, we were able to handle it in the best possible way," he said.
PSD expressed appreciation for his service, saying staff valued the trust he had placed in them to contribute ideas, shoulder responsibilities and drive reforms together.
It said the collaborative spirit he had fostered would guide the department in challenging conventional practices and making public services more accessible.
Deputy Public Service director-general (Development) Datuk Dr Mohd Bakhari Ismail and deputy Public Service director-general (Operations) Datuk Mohd Shaiful Ibrahim attended the farewell ceremony, Majlis Lambaian Bakti, alongside the department's senior management and staff.
Wan Ahmad Dahlan will continue as chairman of Malaysia Rapid Transit Corporation Sdn Bhd (MRT Corp), a position he was appointed to on Aug 13 this year.
He will also continue as chairman of the Sustainable Energy Development Authority (SEDA Malaysia), to which he was appointed on May 15 last year.
Meanwhile, his successor has yet to be announced.
The post is among the most critical in the federal administration, overseeing public sector human resource management and driving civil service reforms.
It is traditionally filled by
senior civil servants
with extensive government administration experience, particularly those who have served as secretary-general in major ministries.

Title: DNeX names Vinie Chong group CEO after five months in interim role
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Dagang NeXchange Bhd (DNeX) has named Vinie Chong Pui Ling as group chief executive officer (CEO), formalising her leadership after more than five months overseeing the company on an interim basis.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing, DNeX said Chong, 47, had been redesignated as group CEO effective Nov 19, while retaining her position as group chief financial officer (CFO).
Chong was redesignated as group chief operating officer in May before taking charge of the company on an interim basis following the resignation of former group CEO Faizal Sham Abu Mansor in June.
Faizal resigned on June 3 due to personal commitments. DNeX said there was no disagreement with the board.
Chong has more than 20 years of experience in financial management, commercial operations and strategic planning.
Before joining DNeX, she was CFO of Cypark Resources Bhd and group CFO of Cenergi SEA Bhd, a renewable energy company under Khazanah Nasional Bhd.
She also held senior positions at Astro Productions, including CFO and vice-president of strategy and commercial, as well as general manager at Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd.
Chong is also an independent non-executive director of Johor Plantations Group Bhd.

Title: FOI ideas to be evaluated for cabinet consideration, says Zambry
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Ideas gathered at the 2026 Festival of Ideas (FOI) will be evaluated, with the best proposals to be presented to the cabinet for consideration, Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir said.
He said FOI brought together experts and thought leaders to exchange views and contribute to the country's development, while generating ideas that could also benefit the wider world.
"The views and ideas put forward will be evaluated before being brought to the cabinet for consideration, and we will make our recommendations," he told reporters after the closing ceremony today.
He said the third edition of FOI attracted almost 200,000 visitors over three days, describing the turnout as a source of pride and a sign of the event's growing international recognition.
"We hope this initiative will continue from time to time and not stop here. As I have said repeatedly, I hope it will continue even after I am no longer the minister.
"I am not implying anything, but this is a major programme for the country," he said.
Meanwhile, Malaysian Qualifications Agency (MQA) chief executive officer Professor Datuk Dr Mohammad Shatar Sabran said the agency would shortlist the 20 most-voted ideas submitted through the Wall of Ideas and present them to Zambry for consideration.
He said MQA, in collaboration with Education Malaysia Global Services, was using an artificial intelligence-powered platform to collect, categorise and rank ideas submitted by festival visitors.
"If suggestions can be implemented immediately, for example, specific fields that should be offered at university level, we will pass them to the institutions to decide which programmes are suitable.
"Some ideas are easy to realise, while others may require policies at national or ministry level.
"We will see how it goes. I think this is the best method, as people can share their views without feeling shy because they are using their own phones," he said.
The Wall of Ideas at FOI 2026 is the Higher Education Ministry's first open platform for the public to contribute ideas and suggestions towards a more progressive, inclusive and sustainable Malaysia.
Visitors can share their views under five themes: Nation and Governance; Knowledge, Innovation and the Future; Economy and Industry; Sustainability and Well-being; and National Security and Resilience.

Title: DNeX swings to RM58.6mil Q3 net profit on semiconductor recovery
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Dagang NeXchange Bhd (DNeX) returned to profitability in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 with a net profit of RM58.6 million against RM10.6 million a year earlier.
This was driven by a strong turnaround in its semiconductor business.
DNeX's revenue rose 11 per cent year-on-year to RM297 million, while profit attributable to owners increased to RM42.6 million from RM12 million previously.
Earnings per share improved to 1.22 sen from 0.35 sen.
For the nine months, DNeX's net profit reached RM103.5 million against a net loss of RM71.6 million.
The previous year's results included a one-off, non-cash deferred tax charge of RM95.5 million arising from changes to the United Kingdom's Energy Profits Levy.
Its nine-month revenue increased to RM849.4 million from RM826.7 million, while cash generated from operations more than doubled to RM238.9 million from RM88.8 million.
DNeX's semiconductor division was the main earnings driver, recording a pre-tax profit of RM43.9 million against a loss of RM13.8 million a year earlier.
Its revenue surged 36 per cent to RM204 million, supported by higher shipment volumes of 51,000 wafers against 46,000 previously and a better product mix.
Emerging technology products accounted for 62 per cent of segment revenue, up from 40 per cent a year earlier.
The energy division also returned to profitability, posting a pre-tax profit of RM8.1 million against a loss of RM1.9 million, despite lower revenue of RM54.2 million due to planned oilfield maintenance.
Group chief executive officer Vinie Chong Pui Ling said it was benefiting from strategic consolidation, cost optimisation and a shift towards higher-value semiconductor products.
DNeX maintained a net cash position as at Sept 30, with cash balances of RM546.5 million against borrowings of RM172.1 million.
Chong said the company's focus was on translating operational improvements into sustainable earnings growth, supported by disciplined capital allocation and a stronger balance sheet.

Title: New UiTM vice-chancellor expected to be appointed soon, says Zambry
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A new vice-chancellor for Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) is expected to be appointed soon, with the selection process already under way, Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir said.
He said the Public University Vice-Chancellor Selection Committee was carrying out the necessary procedures, including advertising the vacancy, selecting candidates and conducting interviews.
"We are now going through the necessary steps, which include advertising the post, selection and interviews.
"The process will not take long, as the vacancy needs to be filled," he told reporters after the closing ceremony of the 2026 Festival of Ideas here today.
The position became vacant following the end of Prof Datuk Dr Shahrin Sahib @ Sahibuddin's tenure as the university's seventh vice-chancellor on Nov 3.
Shahrin, an expert in cybersecurity, networks, computer systems and parallel processing, completed his three-year tenure after being appointed on Nov 2, 2023.
In the meantime, Deputy Vice-Chancellor Prof Dr Yamin Yasin is serving as acting vice-chancellor.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia draws RM9.2bil in indicative investment proposals from China – Anwar
Article:
SHENZHEN: Malaysia has secured indicative investment proposals worth RM9.2 billion following meetings with China-based companies during Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's visit to the country for the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting.
Anwar said the figure remained indicative, with further details of the proposed investments to be provided by the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) at a later date.
"(The investment proposals total) RM9.2 billion, that is the figure so far," he told a press conference after attending the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting here today.
He said more than seven companies were involved in the meetings during the working visit, including Fast Print Circuit Tech, Fast Train Technology, Mandarin Biomedical, Jinci Material and Capture Technology, as well as companies in the new energy materials sector.
The proposed projects span several states, including Kedah, Penang, Selangor and Pahang. The Federal Government will also help expedite the implementation process to support the interests of the states involved.
Anwar said the meetings were held in collaboration with the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI), MIDA, the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (MATRADE) and the Malaysian Embassy in China.
"Malaysia is also encouraging these companies to expand their activities here, while creating more opportunities for Malaysian products to be exported to the Chinese market," he said.
Anwar said trade ties with China were particularly important, with bilateral trade reaching RM541.15 billion in 2025.
He said the importance of the economic relationship extended beyond large corporations, benefiting small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and supporting tens of thousands of jobs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MPI's Q1 profit slips 9.5pct on stronger ringgit, higher depreciation charges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd's (MPI) net profit fell 9.5 per cent to RM48 million in the first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q1 FY27), from RM53.05 million a year ago.
This was due to the strengthening of the ringgit and higher depreciation charges.
However, MPI's revenue for the quarter rose 23.7 per cent to RM785.28 million from RM634.84 million previously.
The company said revenue from its Asia, US and Europe segments increased by 19 per cent, 68 per cent and four per cent respectively, against the corresponding quarter last financial year.
Earnings per share declined to 24.10 sen from 26.70 sen a year ago, MPI's filing with Bursa Malaysia today showed.
MPI remains confident in its growth prospects, particularly in artificial intelligence (AI) servers and the recovering automotive sector.
It will remain focused on cost optimisation initiatives to mitigate rising production costs amid global economic challenges and geopolitical uncertainties.
Barring any unforeseen circumstances, MPI expects its performance for the financial year to be satisfactory.

Title: YNH Property director quits amid board dispute over financial records, property probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: YNH Property Bhd non-independent non-executive director Datuk Yu Kuan Chon has resigned amid a board dispute over access to financial records and investigations into property transfers involving a subsidiary.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing, YNH said Yu, 64, claimed he had been denied access to information needed to discharge his duties as a director and disagreed with the board's refusal to provide details of the group's accounts.
The board clarified that Yu had been placed on administrative leave on Oct 29 as a precautionary measure, pending investigations into property transfers involving a subsidiary.
It said the decision was made because Yu was an interested director in the matter, which involved the transfer of certain properties without receipt of the purchase consideration.
"This matter was first raised with him in April, before his requests for information, and a police report was lodged on Sept 12," the company said.
"During the administrative leave, his access to the group's records and documents was limited subject to the prior written approval of the board."
Yu's resignation comes after YNH disclosed in its lates annual report, released last month, that an audit had uncovered discrepancies between the registered ownership of certain investment properties and the group's accounting records.
A subsequent board review identified transactions involving a former executive director, prompting the group to lodge a police report in September.
The annual report also disclosed that nine investment property units had been transferred in May 2024 under a sale and purchase agreement valued at RM7.52 million.
The disposal had not been recorded in the group's accounts, and no evidence of receipt of the stated payment had been identified.
Further reviews identified 12 completed property units that had been transferred in previous financial years but remained recorded as inventories.
Separately, YNH said Yu had raised issues concerning remuneration, statutory contributions and advances he claimed to have made to the group.
The company disputed his account and said it would examine these matters separately.
Yu previously served as YNH's executive chairman before relinquishing the position in December 2024 to "spend more time with his family", according to an earlier filing.
He remained an executive director until December 2025, when he was redesignated as a non-independent non-executive director.
Yu is the brother of YNH executive chairman Datuk Yu Kuan Huat and uncle of managing director Yu Kai Leun and executive director Yu Kai Liang.
Following his resignation, the resolution seeking Yu's re-election at the company's annual general meeting on Nov 24 will be withdrawn.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar accepts Ahmad Maslan's apology over inappropriate remark
Article:
SHENZHEN: Cabinet members who use inappropriate language against another member or the government should resign, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Referring to Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan's slip-up in the Dewan Rakyat, Anwar said he understood that heightened political tensions, particularly during election campaigns, could sometimes lead to the use of inappropriate language.
However, he said such conduct should not be brought into official government proceedings.
"If anyone violates this principle in the future, they should resign or be advised to resign because our system cannot function that way. If there is disagreement, it can be raised at cabinet meetings.
"If a decision needs to be changed, it can be brought up at the appropriate forum," he said.
Anwar, however, accepted Ahmad's apology over the incident.
"But in this particular case, I thank him and appreciate the positive spirit he has shown," he told a media conference after attending the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting here today.
Anwar also thanked Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi for addressing the matter to ensure that decorum within the government administration and mutual respect among cabinet members were upheld.
It was reported that Ahmad, who is also the Pontian member of Parliament, had reportedly apologised to
the prime minister
for using the word "kena kencing" in a pantun during the winding-up session of his ministry's debate in the Dewan Rakyat on Nov 16.
In a letter dated Nov 17, Ahmad admitted that his choice of word in the pantun he recited was inappropriate for someone holding a position in the government.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pos Malaysia's indirect unit to sell bulk carrier for RM52.7mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pos Malaysia Bhd's indirect wholly owned subsidiary PNSL Bhd has entered into a memorandum of agreement (MoA) with Hong Kong-based WYW Co Ltd to dispose of its bulk carrier MV Pos Logistics 1 (PL1) for US$12.9 million (RM52.7 million) cash.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, Maybank Investment Bank Bhd, on behalf of Pos Malaysia's board of directors, said PNSL entered into the MoA on Nov 18, 2026, subject to the terms and conditions of the agreement.
WYW is principally engaged in vessel chartering, ship management, crew manning and cargo transportation, supplemented by container liner and oil tanker operations.
It said the Malaysian-flagged vessel was built in 2011 and has a deadweight tonnage of 93,226. It is currently held for disposal and is not deployed in operations.
"PNSL purchased the vessel on Aug 11, 2017 at a cost of US$18.1 million.
"The vessel had an audited net book value of US$15.6 million as at Dec 31, 2025 and an unaudited net book value of US$12.2 million as at Sept 30, 2026," it added.
Pos Malaysia said the proposed disposal would allow the company to unlock and realise the value of its investment in PL1, which forms part of its non-core business, while eliminating the costs and resources associated with its continued retention.
Barring any unforeseen circumstances, the proposed disposal is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of 2026, it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KJTS Group bags RM48mil subcontract for hyperscale data centre in Port Dickson
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: KJTS Group Bhd has secured a RM48 million subcontract from Gamuda Engineering Sdn Bhd to undertake mechanical works for a hyperscale data centre in Port Dickson, Negri Sembilan.
The project, awarded to its subsidiary KJ Technical Services Sdn Bhd, involves a data centre being developed for a multinational technology company headquartered in the United States.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, KJTS said the contract covers the engineering, procurement, manufacturing, delivery, installation, testing and commissioning of mechanical systems.
The scope also includes the supply of materials, equipment and labour, as well as supervision, maintenance and servicing works.
The project will be completed in two phases, with the first scheduled for substantial completion by Oct 22, 2027, followed by the second on Jan 21, 2028.
KJTS said the contract was expected to contribute positively to the group's earnings and net assets over its duration.

Title: PM wants thorough probe into student's death at MCKK, findings made public
Article:
SHENZHEN: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the Education Ministry to thoroughly investigate the cause of death of a
Form Three student
at Malay College Kuala Kangsar, with the findings to be made public.
Anwar said he had discussed the incident with the police and Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, describing it as something completely beyond his comprehension.
"This is a matter that deeply disturbs us. May Allah SWT protect us and remind us all - parents, peers and friends - that this is an issue we must address together as one big Malaysian family," he said during a press conference after attending the 2026 Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting.
He called for a more transparent and independent investigation to determine the actual cause of the incident.
"It could be family problems, issues with parents, problems with friends, whatever the problem may be, for it to reach this point is truly heartbreaking and devastating," he said.
The death should serve as a reminder to all parties of the importance of shared responsibility in ensuring the well-being of children, he added.
Anwar also questioned the level of monitoring and care provided for students in fully residential schools, particularly when a student is absent from class or in areas such as the sick bay.
"In a fully residential school, based on my experience, things are monitored. If someone doesn't attend class, they are indeed in the sick bay. In fully residential schools, there is a dedicated temporary space for care in the sick bay.
"But how could it be that no one was watching the sick bay?" he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar: Nothing unusual about declassification of Najib pardon documents
Article:
SHENZHEN: There is nothing extraordinary about the declassification of documents concerning Datuk Seri Najib Razak's pardon, as such documents are usually declassified when challenged in court, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said the original documents issued by the Pardons Board were classified as secret, but their declassification was not unusual if they became the subject of court proceedings.
He said applications or legal challenges involving such documents could normally lead to their declassification, while the date of declassification would be determined later.
"The order document for Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest is classified under the Official Secrets Act. However, as a general principle, if the order had been challenged and brought to court, it would have been declassified," he said.
Anwar was commenting on reports concerning the minutes of a Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting, which discussed granting house arrest to the former prime minister and have since been declassified.
However, he stopped short of confirming whether the house arrest order document had also been declassified, saying he had only learned about the matter yesterday and had not been following it closely.
He said he could refer any further questions to the cabinet, as he had not followed the matter in detail.
"What I know is that the original documents were classified as secret, but they are usually declassified when brought before the court.
"The same thing happened in my case. The documents were initially classified as secret, but once there was a court challenge, they had to be declassified. In my case, I did not challenge the Pardons Board's decision, but the process. So, this is nothing unusual," he said.
Anwar was referring to his own pardon in 2018 by the then Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Muhammad V. The relevant documents were declassified after the process was challenged in court.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sunway Construction Q3 earnings up 25.4pct, order book hits record RM12.5bil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Construction Group Bhd's net profit rose 25.4 per cent to RM105.06 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM83.78 million a year earlier, supported by contributions from all business segments.
Quarterly revenue, meanwhile, fell 26.2 per cent to RM1.07 billion from RM1.45 billion, mainly due to lower contributions from the construction segment.
For the nine-month period, net profit increased 34.4 per cent to RM327.05 million from RM243.39 million a year earlier, while revenue declined 28 per cent to RM3.11 billion from RM4.32 billion.
Sunway Construction's outstanding order book reached a record RM12.45 billion after securing RM9.80 billion in new contracts so far this year.
The new orders exceeded the upper end of its revised 2026 order book replenishment target of RM7 billion to RM9 billion, following an earlier upward revision from RM6 billion.
The group declared a third interim dividend of 7.9 sen per share, bringing total dividends declared for the first nine months to 34.7 sen per share, including a special dividend of 15.2 sen announced earlier this year.
Group managing director Liew Kok Wing said the record order book provided earnings visibility and a foundation for future growth.
"With RM9.80 billion in new orders secured to date, we have exceeded our revised full-year order book replenishment target, reflecting our clients' confidence in our technical capabilities and ability to deliver mission-critical projects.
"We continue to focus on translating our strong order book into earnings and cash flow through disciplined execution.
"Building on our proven execution track record, we continue to pursue new data centre projects and explore opportunities in other advanced technology facilities, including semiconductor facilities, as well as broaden our geographical presence," he said.
Looking ahead, Liew said the group's priority was to deliver its growing project portfolio on schedule while pursuing contracts with healthy margins to support long-term growth.
"We remain optimistic about the group's performance for the remainder of FY26, supported by our record outstanding order book, strong financial position, expanding technical capabilities, diversified client base across ATFs and the group's projects," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Oil prices rise as Middle East shipping attacks counter supply surplus outlook
Article:
LONDON: Oil prices edged up on Thursday following losses in the previous session as concerns over Middle East supplies amid attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz countered expectations of a market surplus.
Brent crude futures were trading 24 cents, or 0.26 per cent, higher at US$92.19 a barrel at 0953 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate futures for December delivery were up five cents at US$83.31. The December contract expires on Friday, while the more actively traded January contract was up 12 cents at US$82.43.
While uncertainty remained over whether oil prices would see another flare-up or break to the downside, Brent had not been able to stay below US$90 a barrel, PVM Associates analyst John Evans said.
"There is little chance that any solution to both the Ukraine war and Iran conflict being achieved by the trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, but in the small chance something comes of it, entering into fresh length in this current environment does not seem altogether attractive," he said.
US President Donald Trump and his Chinese and Russian counterparts, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, kicked off a three-way meeting, with Trump saying both he and Xi felt strongly that oil had to flow through the Strait of Hormuz.
Still, risks to Middle East oil supplies remained amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Iran's navy said three oil tankers sailing east of the Strait of Hormuz had been disabled by mines, Iranian media reported on Wednesday.
On Thursday, the Iran-aligned Houthi movement fired missiles at the Saudi Arabian capital Riyadh, but the Saudi Civil Defense agency said the danger had passed.
Reuters reported on Wednesday that Ukrainian drone attacks had reduced the combined crude processing volumes of Russian oil refineries by 45 per cent since late October, citing industry sources.
"Intensifying Ukrainian attacks on Russian energy infrastructure are keeping supply risks elevated for both crude oil and products, with production and exports falling," analysts at ANZ said in a note.
However, a larger-than-expected increase in US oil stockpiles reported on Wednesday weighed on the market outlook.
US crude inventories rose by 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million barrels in the week ended Nov 13, the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) said, compared with analysts' expectations in a Reuters poll for an increase of 58,000 barrels.
Brent fell 1.3 per cent in the previous session, while WTI dropped 3.2 per cent to its lowest level since Aug 26 amid growing expectations of a supply surplus.
Prices have also come under pressure from expectations of higher US interest rates, which could weigh on economic growth and slow oil demand growth.
Higher interest rates would also strengthen the US dollar, raising costs for buyers outside the United States who pay for dollar-denominated crude in other currencies.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MNRB Q2 net profit falls 14.8pct on investment losses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MNRB Holdings Bhd's net profit fell 14.8 per cent to RM95.62 million in the second quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM112.27 million a year earlier, weighed down by unrealised fair value losses on its bond and equity investment portfolios.
Quarterly revenue rose 5.8 per cent to RM981.25 million from RM927.58 million, driven by higher insurance and takaful revenue across all business segments, particularly family takaful and retakaful.
For the first half of financial year ending March 31, 2027 (FY27), net profit edged down 0.5 per cent to RM279.37 million from RM280.69 million a year earlier, while revenue increased 4.2 per cent to RM1.98 billion from RM1.90 billion.
MNRB said it continued to strengthen its underwriting capabilities and use data analytics to improve risk assessment and selection, while maintaining disciplined capital deployment amid market volatility.
The group's operating businesses remained key earnings contributors, supported by investments in talent, technical expertise and systems.
Looking ahead, MNRB said it remained cautiously optimistic about its prospects for the second half of FY27 despite a competitive market environment.
The group plans to strengthen its core businesses and pursue selected growth opportunities in Malaysia and overseas as part of its broader transformation strategy.
MNRB aims to become one of Asia's top five reinsurance and retakaful groups within five years by expanding its regional and international presence.
To achieve this, the group plans to invest in talent, specialist capabilities, technology and data analytics while maintaining underwriting discipline and prudent capital allocation.

Title: Ringgit ends higher against greenback following stronger Q3 GDP growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended higher against the US dollar today, boosted by positive market sentiment following Malaysia's stronger gross domestic product (GDP) growth in the third quarter of 2026 (Q3 2026).
At 6pm, the local currency rose to 4.1100/1145 against the greenback from Wednesday's close of 4.1130/1180.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said Q3 2026 GDP growth exceeded the advance estimates, bringing growth for the first nine months of the year to 5.6 per cent from 4.8 per cent in the corresponding period last year.
"Against this backdrop, we reiterate that a 25 basis point increase in the overnight policy rate could be considered in early 2027, although slower private consumption growth of 4.3 per cent could pose a challenge to such a decision," he told Bernama.
He said the ringgit's recovery against the US dollar was also supported by bargain hunting among traders.
"Bargain hunting may have set in as traders saw some value and the anticipation of a 50 basis point hike in the US Federal Funds Rate were never a sure thing," he said, adding that the US Dollar Index (DXY) fell 0.11 per cent to 103.752 points.
Yesterday, Bank Negara Malaysia announced Malaysia's economy grew by 5.5 per cent in Q3 2026 against 5.3 per cent in the same quarter of 2025, driven by continued household spending, higher investment activity and stronger exports.
The central bank said export growth strengthened further, driven by technology-related exports across both electrical and electronics (E&E) and non-E&E products.
At the close, the ringgit traded mostly higher against a basket of major currencies.
It rose against the Japanese yen to 2.5705/5735 from 2.5826/5859 at Wednesday's close, went up vis-à-vis the British pound to 5.4034/4093 from 5.4172/4238 but edged down against the euro to 4.5181/5231 from 4.5144/5199.
The ringgit traded mixed against its Asean peers.
It appreciated against the Singapore dollar to 3.1870/1908 from 3.1896/1937, gained vis-à-vis the Indonesian rupiah to 225.1/225.4 from 225.6/225.9, but slipped against the Thai baht to 12.1232/1411 from 12.1138/1339. The local note was almost flat against the Philippine peso to 6.45/6.46 from 6.45/6.47.

Title: Anwar: Malaysia's participation in Apec China reinforces centrality, foreign policy independence
Article:
SHENZHEN: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia's participation in the Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting builds on the country's centrality and independent economic and foreign policy in an increasingly fragmented world.
Following the highly productive trip, Anwar's sixth since becoming prime minister, Malaysia reaffirmed its non-aligned, open-trade stance through bilateral and informal meetings with global leaders.
Among these was a meeting with US President Donald Trump, following up on their previous meeting in Manila.
Anwar said Trump's colleagues, including Secretary Marco Rubio and Jamieson Greer, had emphasised the need to maintain ties to ensure that American trade and investment in Malaysia, as well as overall trade relations with the United States, remained unaffected.
The meeting also served as an assurance that Malaysia's good relations with China would not compromise its interests as an independent nation, he said.
Anwar said his attendance, together with Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution and the secretary-general, was at the invitation of Chinese President Xi Jinping.
"We took advantage of the opportunity to hold a bilateral meeting with him. Although we had already met earlier this year, this demonstrates the growing strength of our good relations and friendship with China," he said.
Anwar also held a brief meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin, where discussions centred on preliminary agreements on trade, energy procurement and security, as well as the export of diesel, oil and gas.
The prime minister said a key pillar of Malaysia's economic strategy remained its vital relationship with China.
Trade between the two nations surpassed half a trillion ringgit, reaching RM541.15 billion in 2025.
Building on this momentum, the government had secured RM9.2 billion in potential investments from major regional technology and manufacturing firms.
Among the corporations expanding their footprint in hubs across Kulim Hi-Tech, Penang, Selangor and Pahang are Fastprint Circuit Tech, Fast Train Technology, Mindray Biomedical and New Energy Materials.
Anwar reiterated the government's commitment to facilitating these investments by cutting red tape while ensuring local small and medium enterprises (SMEs) were integrated into the supply chain and protected from predatory foreign takeovers.
Malaysia's economic trajectory continued to outperform projections, recording gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 5.5 per cent in the third quarter of 2026.
Anwar said the growth reflected the success of ongoing economic and foreign policy initiatives.
"Historically, we often meet our projections, but it is rare for us to exceed them so positively," he said.

Title: PM reveals RMAF officers, pilots involved in drug trafficking
Article:
SHENZHEN: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has revealed that Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) personnel, including pilots, are implicated in a drug smuggling case involving large quantities of narcotics.
He said the case was troubling and warned that action must be taken against those involved, regardless of rank.
Speaking at his exit press conference here, Anwar said police and the Armed Forces needed some time to complete their investigations.
"I am saying this at this press conference because I do not want anyone to think that we are deliberately delaying action," he said.
Anwar said those implicated included officers at the ranks of lieutenant and captain, as well as pilots.
"How can we expect the country to be safe if we allow this to happen?" he said.
"This is the security forces. It is like 'harapkan pagar, pagar makan padi'," he said, referring to the Malay proverb about those entrusted with protection betraying that trust.
Anwar said he had discussed the matter with the Inspector-General of Police, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin, the Chief of Defence Forces and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said all parties agreed that there should be no compromise in taking action.
"This is not about protecting the image of any department," he said, adding that police should be given room to complete their probe.
Anwar said the government had also acted against organised groups involved in drug trafficking and abuse of the financial system, with more than 100 people detained under the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act and billions of ringgit in assets seized or frozen.
He said such action showed that the government was serious about tackling drug smuggling and related criminal activity.
"The country cannot allow this kind of misconduct to continue, whether it involves those at the highest levels, civil servants or enforcement personnel," he said.
